results.title: Smart Healthcare at Home: A Review of AI-Enabled Wearables and ...
results.content: To evaluate the usability and adoption potential of emerging home-based health technologies, this review applies the Pi-CON methodology, a human-centered framework for assessing passive, non-contact and continuous monitoring systems with minimal user burden for data collection. These works, together with its adoption by other researchers, establish Pi-CON as a practical approach for evaluating the real-world integration of AI-enabled, home-based health monitoring solutions. One of the most critical stages in the adoption of home-based health technologies is the onboarding process, meaning the user’s initial experience when setting up and learning how to use a device, app, or system for the first time. AI-enabled wearables and diagnostic tools represent a transformative shift in healthcare delivery, enabling users to engage in real-time, home-based health monitoring. In parallel, design-oriented studies on wearable and ambient health tracking devices [98] and infrastructure-oriented research on RFID and smart sensing networks [99] further highlight how Pi-CON aligns with emerging requirements for unobtrusive, user-centered monitoring.
